rationale: All three required findings are present and correctly framed: sensor drift under high humidity (C2/C9), the restart retry defect (C4), and the explicit conjunctive/necessary-but-not-sufficient structure supported by both comparison runs (C6, C7, C8). No forbidden claims appear — drift-alone and defect-alone are explicitly ruled out, and alert suppression is explicitly placed downstream of the crossing (C10) rather than as an onset cause, matching ground truth. Causal structure (interaction, humidity as mediating/enabling condition for the drift arm, suppression as a duration-only effect) is represented without inventing unsupported mechanism detail; where the mechanism is genuinely unclear (e.g., how an upward-reading drift yields an over-limit outcome), this is correctly left as an open uncertainty (U1) rather than asserted. Evidence discipline is strong: every claim cites specific evidence IDs, no outside facts are introduced, and misleading/ambiguous evidence (e.g., the drift-direction puzzle, timeout occurrence) is flagged rather than glossed over. Uncertainty calibration is excellent, with multiple live alternatives (CF1–CF6), discriminating observations tied to each uncertainty, and appropriately hedged confidence levels. Action quality closely tracks the preferred action: A1 (fix restart logic) and A2 (recalibrate/harden sensors) target the two necessary mechanisms and are correctly prioritized over A3 (alerting fix, explicitly treated as secondary/non-preventive) and diagnostic-only monitoring/probe actions. No harmful, irrelevant, or protective-control-weakening actions are proposed, and no condition-identification or outside-evidence issues are present.
